transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-13
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (OrbitHealth Procurement), Rajiv Narayan (OrbitHealth Legal), Claire Dumas (Platform), Tom Park (Security), Elena Ruiz (Finance)

Summary:
High-level procurement and legal intake covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations for a private/dedicated deployment, exception matrix for onboarding, and POC timelines. OrbitHealth emphasized data residency (EU), KMS controls, and a short procurement window. Redwood AE/SE walked through typical exceptions, canary rollback policy, and suggested SLA tiers.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and exception matrix
- DPA data residency and KMS/HSM integration
- SLA tiers for latency/uptime and financial remedies
- Pricing approval path and PO timing
- POC scope: private VPC vs dedicated pool

Action items (brief): see metadata list above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood, i think we have about an hour. quick intros?
[00:08] Maya: Hi Maya here procurement at OrbitHealth, we run vendor intake for platform tools.
[00:11] Claire: Claire, head of platform on the call.
[00:13] Rajiv: Rajiv, legal.
[00:15] Tom: Tom security.
[00:17] Elena: Elena finance.
[00:19] Samir: Great, Lena will do the technical bits, i'm keeping notes on the commercial exceptions. Noah's on to help with onboarding timelines.
[00:28] Lena: hi all, just to set expectations i'll cover architecture options — hosted vs dedicated vs private — and typical guardrails we surface in the MSA, then we can map to orbit's requirements.
[00:38] Claire: quick note, our core requirement is EU data residency and we need KMS with customer-managed keys for PHI-workloads.
[00:46] Lena: understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations, we call that out in the private deployment docs, there are a few operational caveats re key rotation windows and backup/export.
[00:57] Tom: what's the encryption in transit story? we use TLS 1.3, mutual TLS for service-to-service, and we need audit logs forwarded to our splunk.
[01:05] Lena: TLS 1.3 supported, mutual TLS possible for private; audit logs can be exported to S3 or pushed via syslog — note sometimes the field names vary depending on runtime, so we usually supply a mapping doc.
[01:18] Rajiv: on the MSA, first pass we saw two items: indemnity cap and data processing carveouts for law enforcement. also need clarity on subprocessor list and 30-day notification for new subprocessors.
[01:31] Samir: thanks Rajiv, yes on subprocessors we provide list and a 30-day notice by default; we can consider contractual carveouts but we try to keep substitution flexibility. on indemnity, we can discuss a carve-in for willful misconduct but our standard cap sits at x months of fees — we can add that to the exceptions matrix.
[01:46] Maya: procurement timeline — we have a standing committee that votes next Wednesday, ideally we'd have pricing and legal responses before then otherwise it'll go to next cycle.
[01:55] Elena: correct, finance needs a PO and agreed payment terms by 2025-06-25 to hit our fiscal cut-off.
[02:03] Samir: ok we can target sending redlines and a pricing summary by 2025-06-18 to give you time.
[02:09] Claire: for SLA, our apps need 99.9% runtime for production and p99 latency under 300ms for a 512 token prompt; do you have verified numbers?
[02:21] Lena: so a few nuances — hosted offerings can meet that for average loads, but for strict p99 and throughput at scale we recommend Redwood Dedicated with a pinned pool. we publish benchmarks but the p99 depends on sequence length and KV cache hit rates. we can run a quick runbook against a sample prompt set.
[02:38] Tom: and if you can't meet SLA what are remedies? credits or failovers?
[02:42] Samir: typical is service credits tied to downtime windows, and we recommend an automatic fallback to a regional compatible model. we can also include a canary/rollback policy in the runbook.
[02:52] Rajiv: service credits are fine but need to see caps and measurement method (what counts as an outage). also, do you have SOC2? ISO?
[02:59] Samir: we are SOC 2 Type II and pursuing ISO 27001, we'll attach attestation; for measurement we propose synthetic probes + customer telemetry counts as SLA measurement.
[03:13] Maya: procurement also flagged data residency proof — do you have region-specific hosting and contractual guarantees?
[03:20] Lena: yes, private deployment with a customer control plane in eu-west-1 or on-premises for air-gapped. Contractually we can add a data residency clause with restrictions on cross-border replication except for disaster recovery with prior notice.
[03:35] Elena: for KMS, we require customer-managed keys and an HSM-backed KMS ideally with no export capability. can you support bring-your-own-key?
[03:44] Lena: we support BYOK via HSM/KMS integrations in private deployments. small caveat: certain automatic snapshot features will create encrypted backups but we can exclude KMS export by policy. we'll include technical steps in the onboarding doc.
[03:58] Claire: about subprocessors — any third-party model providers (like foundations) you use, are they considered subprocessors and do we get visibility?
[04:07] Samir: yes any external model hosting or data processing partners are in the subprocessor list; we can provide a redline-friendly list. sometimes model vendor contracts restrict detailed disclosure, but we commit to notify and share summaries.
[04:21] Rajiv: DPA: we need a standard EU Data Processing Addendum with SCCs. can you commit to SCCs and allow us to execute the DPA with minor edits?
[04:30] Samir: yes SCCs are included and our DPA is generally addendum-friendly; we prefer tracked edits but we will be responsive.
[04:37] Maya: back to pricing — we want a dedicated pool quote vs hosted for a projected 10M tokens/month. finance prefers a committed monthly rate to get discounting.
[04:48] Samir: we can do committed reserved capacity for Dedicated; Lena can sketch the throughput mapping to GPU pools. discounts scale with commit length 6/12/24 months.
[04:58] Elena: also need clarity on egress costs for model updates and if snapshots incur storage fees.
[05:05] Noah: on storage, snapshot retention beyond a certain window may incur charges; we'll include a clear table. for model updates, if we push large weights there's a one-off transfer cost for on-prem prep.
[05:17] Lena: technical POC approach suggestion: 2-week pilot in a private VPC, we deploy a small dedicated pool with sample prompt set, measure p50/p95/p99 and token throughput, validate KMS integration and audit log exports.
[05:29] Claire: two weeks is tight but acceptable for an initial performance vet. we also want security to run a quick run of the questionnaire.
[05:36] Tom: yes security questionnaire is a hard blocker — we'll need to confirm posture on access controls and privileged keying.
[05:43] Lena: we'll provision a limited access test environment and include role-based access controls with SSO/SAML integration. note that some privileged workflows (like key rotation) require coordination with OrbitHealth ops.
[05:55] Rajiv: if there are certain MSA clauses you won't accept, can you enumerate them? we prefer a table with R/Y/G (reject/yes/gray) statuses.
[06:03] Samir: absolutely — we'll produce an exception matrix with three columns: clause, Redwood position, proposed language. that'll make your legal triage faster.
[06:11] Maya: procurement also asked whether Redwood will accept a vendor assurance letter for some low-risk items or if you require full contract redlines.
[06:19] Samir: for low-risk things sometimes a vendor attestation suffices, but anything that touches customer data or keys usually needs contractual language. we'll note which items can be handled via attestation.
[06:30] Elena: final commercial ask from finance: net-45 payment terms are preferred; do you accept net-45 for enterprise customers?
[06:37] Samir: we typically do net-30 but can review net-45 on committed multi-year deals; we'll flag that in the commercial term sheet.
[06:45] Claire: one more technical: how do you handle model version pinning for regressions? we want deterministic model outputs across versions in production.
[06:52] Lena: you can pin model hash and version; Redwood supports rollbacks and A/B rollouts with traffic fractions. we also keep model artifacts in immutably tagged storage for reproducibility. small gotcha: quantized builds may differ slightly, we capture evaluation diffs.
[07:08] Rajiv: ok let's agree to next steps and a timeline.
[07:11] Samir: recap: Redwood to send MSA/DPA redlines + exception matrix by 2025-06-18; Redwood SE to deliver POC performance worksheet and quick private deploy latency run by 2025-06-20; OrbitHealth to provide security questionnaire and procurement decision window by 2025-06-19.
[07:29] Maya: sounds good, i'll try to push internal committee.
[07:32] Elena: i'll confirm PO timing.
[07:34] Samir: great. any other questions?
[07:36] Claire: none from me, thanks.
[07:38] Tom: no, thanks.
[07:39] Rajiv: thanks all.
[07:41] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing.

End of transcript.

References and artifacts mentioned:
- MSA draft (link provided in chat)
- DPA template and SCCs (attached in follow-up)
- POC runbook and performance worksheet (Redwood to deliver)

Note: transcript contains minor transcription errors and occasional speaker mislabels; technical acronyms sometimes split (e.g., K V cache vs KV cache).
